2: What is this information sheet for?
3: In this information sheet, we explain, based on our legal obligation, which rights and obligations you have under your tenancy agreement. Each topic discusses your rights and obligations so that you have a clear and logical overview of them.
5: You can find more information on the following websites:
10: You are renting the dwelling at {{Adres woning}}, {{Plaats woning}}. You share the dwelling with other tenants. This means that they are also entitled to use the dwelling and that the use of the common areas must take place in good consultation. Within the dwelling, you share the following facilities with the other residents: {{Voorzieningen EN}}. The dwelling may be shared by a maximum of {{Max bewoners}} persons.
12: If you stay in the Netherlands for longer than 4 months, you are legally required to register yourself in the Personal Records Database (BRP). Merely registering as a non-resident in the Netherlands is then insufficient.
14: You may not make any alterations to the dwelling. This means, among other things, that you may not paint the walls, stick stickers on the paintwork, or drill into the walls. You must also handle the dwelling’s inventory carefully and with due care.
16: You may only use the rented property for your own residence and related activities. It is prohibited to cause damage to the dwelling (or its furnishings) or nuisance, and/or to use the dwelling for other activities, such as commercial activities and/or (partial) subletting. You must also ensure that other persons do not register themselves at the address of the dwelling in the BRP. If the dwelling is used for other purposes, you will owe a penalty to the landlord. In addition to claiming the penalty, the landlord may also demand performance or dissolution (termination) of the agreement and claim damages. The landlord may also actively monitor this (see section 4 below).
19: Nature of the tenancy agreement and duration of the tenancy
20: The tenancy agreement is a tenancy agreement which, by its nature, is of short duration, in accordance with Section 7:232 paragraph 2 of the Dutch Civil Code. This type of tenancy agreement applies because you wish to rent accommodation temporarily during the period in which you are working in the Netherlands, and you have indicated that after your work ends you will return to your country of origin, where your main residence is and will remain.
22: With a tenancy agreement which by its nature is of short duration, you as a tenant are not entitled to security of tenure, and the landlord is not bound by the exhaustive statutory grounds for termination when ending the tenancy agreement.
24: The tenancy agreement is entered into for a period that is generally equal to the duration of the employment contract, but with a maximum duration of 26 weeks or 6 months. The exact duration of the tenancy agreement is stated in the rent confirmation attached as an appendix to the tenancy agreement. The tenancy cannot be terminated early unless this is explicitly included in the tenancy agreement.
27: The amount of the rent and the way in which the rent must be paid are included in the rent confirmation. Service costs are included in the rent, and therefore no separate service costs will be charged.
29: A one-time security deposit is also due for the rented property, amounting to four times the weekly rent or one month’s rent obligation. Under the law, the security deposit may amount to a maximum of 2 months’ base rent, so the security deposit you owe remains well within these limits. You must pay this security deposit upon signing the tenancy agreement. You may not offset the final rent instalment(s) against the security deposit.
31: If there is no reason to deduct any amounts from the security deposit, the landlord will return it to you within 14 days after the tenancy agreement ends. You will not receive the security deposit back in full (or at all) if you have caused damage to the dwelling and/or if you have not paid the rent and/or service costs due, or have not paid them in full. If amounts are set off against the security deposit, the landlord will return the remaining amount to you within 30 days after the end of the tenancy agreement. The landlord will provide you in writing with an itemised statement of the deductions from the security deposit. The landlord will repay the (remaining) security deposit to the bank account number known to the landlord.
33: In the exceptional situation where the parties agree to extend the tenancy agreement, the landlord has the right to increase the rent annually in the manner and at the times described in the tenancy agreement. If this occurs, you will receive a separate notice from us.
35: More information about rent increases can be found here: Which rules apply to a rent increase? | Government of the Netherlands.
38: In principle, the landlord does not have the right to enter your dwelling without your permission. In certain cases, an exception applies. These cases are as follows:
40: In the event of an emergency, such as a gas leak. In that case, the landlord may enter the dwelling without permission;
41: In the event of urgent work on the dwelling, for example work to prevent (further) damage. This also includes, for example, the installation of smoke detectors. In that case, the tenant must give the landlord permission to enter the dwelling;
42: In the event of renovation, work at the neighbours’ dwelling, or a viewing for a new tenant. In these cases, the tenant must give the landlord or workmen permission to enter the dwelling;
43: In the event of inspections of the rented property on the basis of the quality mark of the Stichting Normering Flexwonen.
46: As a tenant, you are responsible for minor maintenance of the dwelling. This means that, for example, if a lamp needs to be replaced, you must do this yourself. For major maintenance or defects in the dwelling, you can contact the landlord. This will be the case, for example, with leaks or when exterior painting or a new central heating boiler is needed.
48: An overview of matters for which you can contact the landlord and those for which you are responsible yourself can be found here: Which costs are for the tenant and which are for the landlord? | Government of the Netherlands
50: It goes without saying that you may not cause damage to your dwelling, to the soft furnishings, furniture and/or inventory present in your dwelling, and/or to the building of which your dwelling forms part. If there is damage to (the interior of) your dwelling or the building of which your dwelling forms part, you are obliged to inform the landlord as soon as possible. You must also ensure that visitors or co-tenants do not cause damage to the dwelling or the building. If you fail to do so, the landlord may impose a penalty on you and/or recover the damage from you.
53: If you have complaints about the dwelling, have identified defects, or have other matters relating to the rented property, you can initially contact the landlord by email at info@ktp.nl, by telephone on 053-7113495 and by regular mail at Kanaalstraat 217, 7547 AS Enschede. The landlord may also appoint a manager. In that case, you should initially contact the manager using the contact details provided for that purpose.
55: If you and the landlord or manager are unable to reach a solution, you can report your complaint to the municipal reporting point for complaints about landlords or letting agents. For your municipality, the reporting point can be reached via: {{Meldpunt}}
57: An overview of municipal reporting points can be found here: Inventory of municipal reporting points and letting regulations (pdf)
59: In some cases, you can also take your complaint to the Rent Tribunal or the subdistrict court. More information can be found here: When can I go to the Rent Tribunal and when to the subdistrict court? | Government of the Netherlands. You should be aware that legislation, reporting points and website links may change from time to time. If you have any questions about this, you can contact the landlord.
